title: Messy skus and category names

brief.decision: Which categories' product records to clean first, so that the category report and the supplier's sku file match again

expected_output.grain: one row per category with at least one product whose sku or category_raw is off, plus one row for the products with a missing category_id

checkpoints.prompt: Sanne says the category report and the supplier's sku file both miss products. How many products have a text key that is off? The products table may hold errors. A sku is off when it is not in standard form: upper case with no spaces anywhere in it. A category_raw is off when it does not equal the category_name of any category, exactly as stored. Count each product once, whether one or both of its keys are off. Type a whole number.
Write the query that answers Sanne's question.

Sanne wants to know how much of the sales data these messy keys touch. How many order lines are of a product whose sku or category_raw is off? These tables may hold errors. A sku is off when it is not in standard form: upper case with no spaces anywhere in it. A category_raw is off when it does not equal the category_name of any category, exactly as stored. Count every order line of such a product, as stored. Type a whole number.

Write an incident note of 2 to 4 sentences for Sanne: what is wrong with the skus and the category names, how many products and sales lines it touches, which category it hits hardest, and what you propose to fix it.

model_plan:
Metric formula: for each category, the number of products whose sku is off and the number whose category_raw is off.
Output grain: one row per category_id with at least one product off, plus one row for the products with a missing category_id.
Tables and keys: products, with categories read for the list of category names; no join on category_id is needed.
Filters: keep the products whose sku differs from its upper-case form with every space removed, or whose category_raw is not one of the category names.
Edge cases: TRIM does not remove a space inside a sku; letter case counts in a sku; a product with a missing category_id still has a category_raw to check and must not be dropped.
Expected row count: 20
model_answer_template: {CP2} products carry a text key that is off: skus in lower case or with spaces, and category_raw values that spell the parent TV & Video in several ways, all of them on one TV category. Together they touch {CP4} order lines, which a report keyed on sku or on category_raw puts under the wrong name or fails to match. Fixing the stored keys is safer than patching every report, but a parent spelling must map back to the product's own child category, not to the parent. Next, upper-case the skus and remove their spaces, and send the TV products with a parent spelling to the master data team to set their child category.
follow_up_question: Which of the products with a missing category_id can be placed in a category from their category_raw alone?
